sentence: This project studies the myeloid cells in brain tumors that suppress the immune system and make immunotherapies work poorly.
This project studies the mechanisms of aging that lie behind the diseases that aging causes.
This project tests whether mutations that happen during fetal development can cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis when no inherited cause is seen.
This project builds a high-pressure freezing instrument that freezes cells and tissues quickly so protein interactions can be imaged.
This project builds shared genetic and molecular resources to study why Alzheimer's disease and related dementias differ between people, especially in Mexican Americans.
This project tests antibodies against a protein called B7-H3 in men with metastatic prostate cancer that no longer responds to hormone treatment.
This project tests ways to find and treat depression and suicidal risk in young people who see pediatric primary care doctors.
This project builds artificial intelligence tools that analyze clinical data and medical images from children with tumors.
This project builds a two-photon imaging tool to study how retinal ganglion cells work and use energy in glaucoma.
This project grows organoids from breast cancer patients to study how breast cancer spreads and resists drugs.
This project studies how epigenetic changes and altered nuclear dynamics in cancer cells help cancer start and progress.
This project builds software that helps researchers annotate several related genomes at once and helps train machine learning systems.
This project teaches researchers in the social and behavioral sciences to use machine learning and artificial intelligence in health research.
This project studies how a long non-coding RNA guides human mesoderm cells to become heart and blood cells.
This project tries to find out which cells in the bone marrow make thrombospondin-1, a factor that ages blood stem cells.
This project tries to find molecular signs that predict heart events and resilience in people with chronic coronary artery disease.
This project tests whether an engineered probiotic bacterium protects intestinal stem cells and reduces gut injury after radiation.
This project studies how group B Streptococcus attaches to the intestinal surface of newborns before it invades the bloodstream.
This project tries to find out how a genetic variant in DNASE1L3 contributes to the autoimmune disease systemic sclerosis.
This project studies how a protein called TEAD3 controls the type of vascular smooth muscle cells.
